extracted.intended_audience: readers and students of art history; architects, sculptors, and historians of medieval/Renaissance building practice
extracted.subtask_description: Descriptive, practice-oriented guidance and evaluative observations about medieval and early-Renaissance Italian architecture and sculpture (foundations, vaulting, church plans, sculptural relief), drawn from Vasari's Lives. Focuses on construction methods, proportions, materials, and design choices that affect durability and aesthetic quality.

rubrics_metrics.name: Support foundations with piles in Pisa
rubrics_metrics.description: These two architects not having much practice of founding in Pisa and therefore not supporting the platform with piles, as they ought, before they had gone halfway with that building it inclined to one side and bent over to the weakest part...
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Always support platforms in Pisa (and similar soft soils) by sinking piles under the foundations; failure to found on piles causes sinking and leaning. Niccola is credited with reintroducing the custom: 'the sinking of piles renders the edifice absolutely safe.'

rubrics_metrics.name: Prefer round/hollow-well plans for tall towers
rubrics_metrics.description: This edifice is round both without and within and built in the shape of a hollow well, and bound together with the stones in a manner that it is well-nigh impossible that it should fall...
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Round, hollow-well construction binds stones together and resists collapse better than square plans for heavy towers; the author asserts that a square version would likely have fallen due to corner stresses.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provide external outworks/encircling foundations for leaning towers
rubrics_metrics.description: It is assisted, above all, by the foundations, which have an outwork three braccia wide outside the tower, made, as it is seen, after the sinking of the campanile, in order to support it.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When a tower is sinking or leaning, build an external outwork (a wide encircling foundation ring) to buttress and stabilize the structure.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid square plans where corner-forces will force walls out
rubrics_metrics.description: I am convinced that if it had been square it would not have been standing to-day, for the reason that the corner-stones of the square sides, as is often seen to happen, would have forced them out in a manner that it would have fallen down.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Be cautious using square plans for slender, heavy towers: corner stones can create outward forces that destabilize the walls; consider circular/octagonal forms instead.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use lightweight vaulting (small tubes and stucco partitions) to reduce wall load
rubrics_metrics.description: In order not to overburden the walls of these buildings the vaulting was made of small tubes and with partitions of stucco...
rubrics_metrics.guidance: To avoid excessive weight on supporting walls, employ lightweight vault construction (e.g., small tubes and stucco partitions). This was a praiseworthy expedient in the period described.

rubrics_metrics.name: Respect classical proportion; avoid extravagant, disproportionate ornament
rubrics_metrics.description: …all with the most strange and extravagant inventions that can possibly be imagined, and not only wide of the good order of the ancients but almost wide of all just and reasonable proportion.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: While inventive ornament may be impressive, deviating excessively from classical orders and reasonable proportion is criticized; strive for balance between innovation and established proportional systems.

rubrics_metrics.name: Design multi-tier churches with clear functional hierarchy and circulation
rubrics_metrics.description: He designed a very beautiful body of a church and convent, making in the model three tiers, one to be made underground and the others for two churches... planning that from the first one should climb to the second by a most convenient flight of steps, which should wind round the principal chapel...
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When planning pilgrimage or multi-level churches, provide clear tiers (e.g., crypt, lower church, upper church) and thoughtful vertical circulation (winding staircases, steps that lead conveniently between levels) to accommodate liturgical and devotional flows.

rubrics_metrics.name: Choose vaulting form for strength (groined vs barrel)
rubrics_metrics.description: He afterwards threw very bold arches, with groined vaulting between one and another. ... they did not make it as has been said, but barrel-shaped, in order that it might be stronger.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Groined vaulting may be architecturally elegant, but in some cases barrel vaulting can be stronger—choose vaulting geometry based on structural demands rather than purely aesthetic preference.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provide stout external towers (buttressing) and spiral staircases for long-term support
rubrics_metrics.description: There were built round the lower church twelve very stout towers, and in each of these a spiral staircase that climbs from the ground up to the summit.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Encircling a vulnerable lower structure with stout buttressing towers (each housing a spiral staircase) can protect the fabric from future ruin and provide access; treat these towers as structural as well as circulation elements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Lay foundations broad, deep, and of suitable material (gravel, lime, great stones)
rubrics_metrics.description: Because of the laying of such foundations for so great a church... very broad and fifteen braccia deep, filling them with good material--namely, with gravel and lime and with great stones below--wherefore... they have been very well able... to support the weight of the great mass of the cupola.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For very large masses (e.g., cupolas), foundations must be both broad and deep and packed with appropriate materials (gravel, lime, large stones) to distribute loads and prevent settlement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provide buttresses at angles to permit taller superstructures
rubrics_metrics.description: Very broad foundations... much consideration was shown in making those buttresses of masonry at every angle of the eight sides, seeing that it was these afterwards that emboldened the mind of Brunellesco to superimpose a much greater weight...
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Masonry buttresses placed at corners/angles strengthen polygonal structures and allow later builders to add greater loads (e.g., domes) with confidence.

rubrics_metrics.name: For very wide naves, use intermediate arches and sloped roofs with gutters to prevent rot
rubrics_metrics.description: Being unable to make the vaulting below the roof by reason of the too great space, he... caused arches to be made from pier to pier, and upon these he placed the roofs on a slope, building stone gutters over the said arches in order to carry away the rain-water, and giving them so much fall as to make the roofs secure, as they are, from the danger of rotting.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When vaulting is impractical across very wide spans, use transverse arches to support sloped roofs; provide stone gutters and adequate roof slope to shed water and avoid timber rot.

rubrics_metrics.name: When local/site constraints or politics intervene, adapt foundations and plan accordingly
rubrics_metrics.description: They insisted... that there should be united and incorporated with the Palace the Tower of the Foraboschi... for which reasons no one must marvel if the foundation of the Palace is awry and out of the square...
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Practical/site/political constraints (pre-existing towers, property disputes) may force departures from ideal plans—document and adapt the foundations and geometry to maintain structural integrity even when the plan is irregular.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reintroduce historically proven techniques from antiquity (imitate good ancient models)
rubrics_metrics.description: There was one... sarcophagus... in very beautiful manner... Niccola... put so much study and diligence into imitating this manner and some other good sculptures that were in these other ancient sarcophagi, that he was judged... the best sculptor of his day.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Study and imitate exemplary ancient precedents (composition, relief treatment) as a way to recover lost skill and improve contemporary practice in sculpture and design.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sculptural technique: deep undercutting / almost wholly detached figures for pictorial effect
rubrics_metrics.description: In this Niccola made many stories of Jesus Christ... with great difficulty almost wholly detached from the marble.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: High-relief and deep undercutting that nearly detach figures from the background create stronger pictorial presence; this technique demonstrates mastery and was highly praised.

rubrics_metrics.name: Narrative clarity and patient workmanship in sculptural panels
rubrics_metrics.description: Carving in it the Universal Judgment, he made therein many figures, if not with perfect design, at least with infinite patience and diligence...
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Sculptural narratives should aim for clarity of story and be executed with diligence; even when design is imperfect, careful workmanship can make a work admirable and effective.

rubrics_metrics.name: Construction/demolition technique: controlled undermining using props
rubrics_metrics.description: Niccola causing the foot of the tower to be cut away on one side and supporting it with wooden props a braccio and a half in length, and then setting fire to them, as soon as the props were burnt away it fell and was almost entirely shattered;
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When intentional demolition is required, controlled removal of support combined with temporary props (later burned away) can bring down a tower safely; this was noted as an ingenious and useful method.

rubrics_metrics.name: Design internal stair and column patterns to balance circulation, visibility, and structural support
rubrics_metrics.description: It is octagonal on the outer side and round within, with stairs that wind in a spiral and lead to the summit, leaving the hollow space in the middle free, in the shape of a well, and on every fourth step are columns that have the arches above them on a slant and wind round and round; wherefore... one goes climbing to the summit in a manner that he who is on the ground always sees all those who are climbing...
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Combine octagonal/external geometry with internal circular wells and spiral staircases; place intermediate columns and slanting arches rhythmically to support vaults while permitting mutual visibility between levels—this balances structural needs with experiential qualities.
